warnings: RULE-4 SWEEP (2026-09-27 rule) — this master was previously unswept (dimension_chains[]/unassigned_dimensions[] absent, confirmed before starting). This staging captures every axis-bearing page's printed x/y/z dimension rows. gridfix.py has NOT been run — every new point below is a raw '@<pos_m>' placeholder, not yet a named dummy line; naming/prime-sequencing/rename-propagation is gridfix's job, not done here.

NEW X-AXIS PLACEHOLDERS FOUND (5): @-1.0 (roof rafter free end, 1.00 m west of grid 1 — printed on S-04 roof_frame_plan หน้า 21, A-04 roof_plan หน้า 06 view2, and the x-axis tail on every elevation/section หน้า 07/08/09), @8.0 (roof rafter free end, 1.00 m east of grid 3, same source set), @3.5 (CX roof-post / อกไก่ ridge centreline offset, 0.50 m west of grid 2 — S-04 ring_beam_plan หน้า 21 view1 only), @-1.3 and @8.3 (underground sanitary pipe-trench boundary, 1.30 m west/east of grids 1/3 respectively — printed identically on SN-04 sanitary plan หน้า 31 view1, EE-03 lighting หน้า 37, EE-04 outlet หน้า 38, M-01 ac/fan หน้า 39).

NEW Y-AXIS PLACEHOLDERS FOUND (5): @-1.0 and @10.5 (roof rafter free ends, 1.00 m north of D / south of A, same source set as the x-axis roof-eave pair above), @3.5 (CX ridge offset, 0.50 m north of row C — S-04 หน้า 21 view1 only, printed with the SAME numeric value 0.50 as the x-offset — coincidence confirmed by re-reading the image, not a transcription duplicate: one tick is horizontal off grid 2, the other vertical off row C), @10.6 (concrete กันสาด ค.ส.ล. canopy slab edge, 1.10 m south of A — S-04 หน้า 21 view1 only), @-1.5 (sanitary pipe-trench boundary, 1.50 m north of D — same 4-sheet source set as @-1.3/@8.3; note the pipe trench is asymmetric — 1.50 m north of D but the south side of the same trench box, verified by direct pixel re-check on หน้า 31, lands exactly on the EXISTING A'/A'' porch/carport points (1.50+1.50), not a third new value — recorded as reuse, not invented).

REVERSES four of the master's own pre-rule-4 'non_grid_dimensions_do_not_confuse' rulings, all deliberately (Makham's rule 4, 2026-09-27, supersedes the old slab/eave/overhang exclusion): entry 'roof eave 1.00 m overhang beyond grids 1/3/D/A' -> now @-1.0/@8.0/@-1.0(y)/@10.5(y); entry 'กันสาด ค.ส.ล. 1.10 m south of row A' -> now @10.6; entry 'ridge line at x=3.50 ... DECISION: no dummy grid' -> now @3.5(x)/@3.5(y); entry 'west side, bathroom 2 step ... 0.60 m strip south of row B ... no dummy grid' -> now B→@6.6 (found this exact tick on หน้า 06 view1, matching the master's own citation 'A-04 left chain 0.60 below B'). The OTHER two non_grid_dimensions entries (1.5 m -> 8.50 slab edge, 3.00 m -> 12.50 carport edge) need NO action: both values already coincide with the EXISTING lines 3''(8.5) and A''(12.5), so nothing new is created there.

TIGHT CLUSTERS — flagged per rule 4's <0.05 m guidance, none merged: (1) x=3.50 (new CX ridge point) sits only 0.05 m from the EXISTING dummy 1''(3.55, carport-edge beam B2). These are genuinely different physical features on different sheets (an isolated roof ridge post vs. a structural carport-edge beam) — kept as two distinct points per 'two ticks with different pos_m are two lines', NOT treated as the same-edge-printed-twice exception. gridfix's prime-ordering will need to interleave them correctly within the 1(0.0)..2(4.0) gap: reading order is @-1.3(new, before origin) / 1(0.0) / 1'(2.55) / @3.5(new) / 1''(3.55) / 2(4.0). (2) South of row A, FOUR points now fall inside the old single A-to-A' 1.50 m gap: A(9.5) / @10.5(new, roof eave) / @10.6(new, canopy edge) / A'(11.0, porch beam, unchanged) — all confirmed as genuinely different physical elements (roof rafter end < concrete canopy slab edge < porch ring-beam), not duplicate readings of one edge. (3) East of grid 3, four points within 1.3 m: 3'(7.6, existing, CN/B4X corner) / @8.0(new, roof eave) / 3''(8.5, existing, SO slab edge) / @8.3(new, pipe-trench boundary) — four different systems (structural corner, roof rafter, ground slab, underground pipe) at the same nominal location, all kept separate. Every one of these clusters needs a human or gridfix's own mismatch-detector to sanity-check before --apply.

z_levels_add carries 4 entries with real printed labels (ระดับพื้นชั้น 1 @0.60 and ระดับหลังอกไก่ @7.15 are genuinely NEW level values, not in the master before this sweep; ระดับหลังคาน @3.75 and ระดับหลังคานหลังคา @4.55 are the SAME level_m values the master already carries under the generic placeholder id 'ระดับ', both appear to be that same un-labelled pair, now found with their real printed names on หน้า 07/08/09). Recommend a human either relabels the two existing generic 'ระดับ' entries in place to match, or accepts these as (label,level_m)-distinct duplicates per the dedup rule — this staging format has no 'edit existing z_levels entry' mechanism, so it is only ADDING, not fixing the label in place.

z-axis dimension_chains: the same 7.15 m total + 4-segment breakdown (0.60/3.15/0.80/2.60) is printed identically on all 6 elevation/section views (รูปด้าน 1-4, รูปตัด 1-2, across หน้า 07/08/09) — recorded as 12 separate chain entries (2 per view: total row + breakdown row) per the 'one entry per printed row per sheet, do not deduplicate' rule, even though every value is identical every time.

NOT converted to a line, recorded in unassigned_dimensions instead: (1) the second CX roof-post's own '0.50' tick near the grid-2/row-B corner (S-04 หน้า 21 view1) — could not confidently tell whether it is a second orthogonal axis offset or the length of a diagonal roof strut/stub; the FIRST CX's two 0.50 ticks WERE clean orthogonal offsets (now @3.5/@3.5) but this one's tick-mark geometry was ambiguous at the resolution available, and rule 4 plus this task's own instruction ('too blurry to read confidently, say so, don't guess') both favour flagging over inventing a direction. (2) the site plan's 11.70 m / 14.60 m lot-boundary dimensions (หน้า 05) — the master's own existing GRID SOURCE PRECEDENCE warning already rules this sheet non-authoritative for grid geometry, and neither number is broken into a segment that ties it precisely to a named grid line (no explicit offset-from-grid1/grid3 value is printed, only a single un-decomposed total), so no dummy line was invented from it. (3) three eave/fascia profile numbers (0.10, 0.40, 0.50 m) repeated on every elevation and section near the roofline — these describe a moulding/fascia board's own cross-section, not a position relative to a grid line.

Deliberately excluded as member/room-internal detail, per rule 4's own carve-out ('a dimension inside one element's own detail ... stays on the element'): WC.1/ห้องน้ำ partition and door-swing dimensions (0.55, 0.25 on หน้า 06), the stair landing depth tag (1.10 near ขึ้น/บันได on หน้า 06, not the same 1.10 as the D-D' grid sub-chain which WAS captured), interior ceiling-height marks (3.00, 2.70 on หน้า 09 รูปตัด 1/2), and every electrical/mechanical device installation-height tag (+1.20M, +1.80M on หน้า 38, spacing '@1.00 ม.' for roof purlins on หน้า 21) and room floor-finish level tags (+0.60/+0.20/+0.50/+0.40/±0.00 boxed room-level codes on หน้า 06/หน้า 05) — the latter are per-room architectural finish levels, not building-wide named z_levels, and are not chained arithmetically to anything, so they were not added to z_levels_add either.

หน้า 06 view1 (floor_plan) carries an extra single-segment y-axis row 'A→A-prime: 1.50' recorded separately from the main south-extension breakdown row — this is a second, physically distinct dimension tick drawn on the right/east side of the plan near เฉลียง, confirmed by image crop, not a duplicate of the west-side breakdown; both are genuinely printed and kept as separate rows.

Two elevations sharing the same physical south-of-row-A edge (รูปด้าน 2 on หน้า 07 vs รูปด้าน 4 on หน้า 08) print DIFFERENT tail values there — รูปด้าน 2 shows 1.00 m (roof eave, reuses @10.5) on both the D-side and A-side, while รูปด้าน 4 shows 1.50 m (porch, reuses A') on the A-side and 1.00 m (roof eave, reuses @-1.0) on the D-side. Both were re-verified directly against the image (not assumed from a single reading) — they are not contradictory, each elevation is dimensioning a different visible edge (roof line vs. porch slab edge) from its own viewing angle. Recorded exactly as printed on each sheet.
